page.notes: The first word of the page reads as a sentence fragment ("multo sale respersas"), so the opening paragraph is marked as continuing from the previous page. The marginal notes "f Epist.84." and "c Orat.2. in Iulianum" stand in the right margin; the note for f is at the mark before "Hieronymo" and is printed in the margin beside the lower lines, so it is placed there by its mark. The text is cut off at the lower edge of this part and continues on the second part of the scan. The side note marked g ("Rerum Rom. li. 11.") stands beside the line of "acceperant" in the right margin; its matching mark is the § before "Eutropius" in the text, which is unclear, so it is printed here as §. The note marked h is placed at the reference mark in the text. The first line is a fragment of a sentence continuing from the previous page. The word "similitèr" is printed with a grave accent on the e, and is transcribed as shown.
